title: BAI (Believable AI Imagery): The Verification-Selection Problem of Low-Salience Synthetic Images
content: This conceptual paper develops Believable AI Imagery (BAI) as an operational concept for fully synthetic images that are visually ordinary, context-compatible, and able to function as documentary or supporting evidence without reliably triggering verification. The central problem is upstream of detection: provenance checks, detectors, and forensic review operate only after an image has been selected for scrutiny. BAI therefore identifies a verification-selection problem in which a mundane synthetic image can acquire evidentiary force from its workflow while remaining too ordinary to be escalated. A May 2026 observation produced mixed outcomes in a 39-image subset. An August 19 follow-up found two AI identifications and five indeterminate results among seven April-generated images, while 30 newly generated, unmodified images were all identified through intact C2PA Content Credentials attributed to OpenAI Media Service. The paper argues that verification intensity should depend on the consequence of error and the availability of independent corroboration, not visual suspicion alone.
